description: Auralith retrieval evaluation set. 28 questions over 3 open-access arXiv papers. Every answer and page label was transcribed by reading the extracted page text of the pinned PDF bytes (see eval/corpus/fetch_corpus.py for SHA-256 pins). Page numbers are 1-indexed and match auralith.ingest.load_pdf, which converts PyPDFLoader's 0-indexed pages.
labelling_notes: relevant_pages lists EVERY page that independently answers the question. Retrieving any one of them counts as a hit, so a fact stated in both an abstract and a results table is not penalised for landing on either.

answer_keys are the specific tokens a correct answer must contain. They are used for a cheap deterministic keyword check that runs alongside the LLM judge, so judge drift can be detected rather than trusted.

type slices the results. 'lexical' questions hinge on a rare exact token and are where BM25 is expected to beat dense retrieval; 'conceptual' questions are paraphrase-heavy and are where dense is expected to win. Stating these predictions up front means Phase C can be evaluated against them rather than rationalised after the fact.

answerable=false questions have no answer anywhere in the corpus. The correct behaviour is to emit NOT_IN_CONTEXT. Without these, a pipeline that confidently fabricates an answer to everything scores identically to one that knows when to stop.

questions.question: How many identical layers are stacked in the Transformer encoder?
questions.answer: Six. The encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers.

questions.question: What BLEU score did the big Transformer model achieve on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task?
questions.answer: 28.4 BLEU, improving over the previous best results (including ensembles) by over 2 BLEU.

questions.question: How many attention heads does the base Transformer use, and what are the key and value dimensions per head?
questions.answer: h = 8 parallel attention heads, with d_k = d_v = d_model / h = 64.

questions.question: What is the inner-layer dimensionality of the position-wise feed-forward network?
questions.answer: d_ff = 2048, while the input and output dimensionality is d_model = 512.

questions.question: Why does scaled dot-product attention divide the dot products by the square root of d_k?
questions.answer: For large values of d_k the dot products grow large in magnitude, which pushes the softmax into regions where it has extremely small gradients. Scaling by 1/sqrt(d_k) counteracts this.

questions.question: What optimizer did the Transformer authors use, and what beta and epsilon values?
questions.answer: Adam, with beta_1 = 0.9, beta_2 = 0.98 and epsilon = 10^-9.

questions.question: How many warmup steps were used in the Transformer learning rate schedule?
questions.answer: warmup_steps = 4000.

questions.question: What hardware were the Transformer base models trained on, and for how long?
questions.answer: One machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs. The base models trained for 100,000 steps, about 12 hours; the big models for 300,000 steps, about 3.5 days.

questions.question: According to the complexity table, what is the maximum path length of a self-attention layer compared to a recurrent layer?
questions.answer: Self-attention has maximum path length O(1); a recurrent layer has O(n). Self-attention also needs O(1) sequential operations versus O(n) for recurrent.

questions.question: What are the layer count, hidden size, attention heads, and total parameters of BERT-BASE and BERT-LARGE?
questions.answer: BERT-BASE: L=12, H=768, A=12, 110M parameters. BERT-LARGE: L=24, H=1024, A=16, 340M parameters.

questions.question: What percentage of WordPiece tokens does BERT mask during masked language model pre-training?
questions.answer: 15% of all WordPiece tokens in each sequence, chosen at random.

questions.question: When BERT selects a token position for masking, how is it replaced?
questions.answer: 80% of the time with the [MASK] token, 10% of the time with a random token, and 10% of the time the token is left unchanged.

questions.question: What tokenization scheme and vocabulary size does BERT use?
questions.answer: WordPiece embeddings with a 30,000 token vocabulary.

questions.question: Which two unsupervised tasks is BERT pre-trained on?
questions.answer: Masked LM (MLM) and Next Sentence Prediction (NSP).

questions.question: What corpora were used to pre-train BERT, and how large were they?
questions.answer: BooksCorpus (800M words) and English Wikipedia (2,500M words).

questions.question: What GLUE score did BERT-LARGE obtain on the official leaderboard, and what did OpenAI GPT obtain?
questions.answer: BERT-LARGE obtained 80.5; OpenAI GPT obtained 72.8 as of the date of writing.

questions.question: What batch size and how many training steps were used for BERT pre-training, and how long did it take?
questions.answer: Batch size of 256 sequences (128,000 tokens per batch) for 1,000,000 steps, roughly 40 epochs over the 3.3 billion word corpus. Each pre-training run took 4 days on 16 Cloud TPUs (64 TPU chips total).
questions.notes: Deliberately buried in Appendix A.2 on page 13, far from the main results. Tests whether retrieval reaches past the abstract and results tables.

questions.question: What are the two RAG model formulations introduced in the paper, and how do they differ?
questions.answer: RAG-Sequence uses the same retrieved document to generate the complete output sequence, while RAG-Token can draw a different latent document for each target token and marginalizes accordingly.

questions.question: Which retriever and which generator does RAG use?
questions.answer: The retriever is DPR (Dense Passage Retriever), a BERT-BASE bi-encoder; the generator is BART-large.

questions.question: How many parameters does the BART-large generator used in RAG have?
questions.answer: 400M parameters (the paper gives 400M on p.3 and the more precise 406M on p.18).

questions.question: Which Wikipedia dump does RAG index, how is it chunked, and how many documents result?
questions.answer: The December 2018 dump. Each article is split into disjoint 100-word chunks, totalling 21M documents.

questions.question: What library and approximation does RAG use to build its MIPS index?
questions.answer: FAISS, with a Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) approximation for fast retrieval.

questions.question: During RAG training, which components are fine-tuned and which are held fixed?
questions.answer: The query encoder BERT_q and the BART generator are fine-tuned. The document encoder BERT_d and the document index are kept fixed, because updating the document encoder would require periodically re-indexing all documents.

questions.question: What are the two decoding procedures RAG-Sequence uses called?
questions.answer: Thorough Decoding and Fast Decoding.

questions.question: In the index hot-swapping experiment, how accurately did RAG answer questions about world leaders when the index year matched the question year, and when it did not?
questions.answer: 70% correct using the 2016 index for 2016 leaders and 68% using the 2018 index for 2018 leaders. With mismatched indices accuracy collapsed to 12% (2018 index, 2016 leaders) and 4% (2016 index, 2018 leaders).

questions.question: BERT's architecture is based on the Transformer encoder from an earlier paper. Which paper is that, and how many layers did that paper's base encoder stack use?
questions.answer: Vaswani et al. (2017), 'Attention Is All You Need'. Its base encoder used a stack of N = 6 identical layers.
questions.notes: Requires joining a citation in bert.pdf p3 to the architecture detail in attention.pdf p3. Scored as a hit if either document's page 3 is retrieved, but a fully correct answer needs both.

questions.question: What BLEU score did the Transformer achieve on the WMT 2014 English-to-Romanian translation task?
questions.answer: NOT_IN_CONTEXT
questions.notes: The paper reports English-to-German and English-to-French only. Phrased to look exactly like attn-002 so a pipeline that pattern-matches on 'BLEU score ... WMT 2014' will confidently fabricate a number.

questions.question: How many US dollars did it cost to pre-train BERT-LARGE?
questions.answer: NOT_IN_CONTEXT
questions.notes: The paper reports TPU-days and references preemptible TPU pricing but never states a dollar cost. Nearby-but-absent facts are the realistic failure case.
